blocks.text: Who reads open Arab sources meets every day names of institutions, offices, acts and titles: ⁧مَجْلِسُ النُّوَّابِ⁩ , ⁧رَئِيسُ الحُكُومَةِ⁩ , ⁧مَرْسُومٌ رِئَاسِيٌّ⁩ , ⁧دَخَلَ حَيِّزَ التَّنْفِيذِ⁩ , ⁧مَعَالِي الوَزِيرِ⁩ . In this unit you learn the basic vocabulary of the State (the three powers, the government and ministries, parliaments, the judiciary in general terms), local administration, official acts and international organizations, with differences between Arab countries and the protocol titles. Above all, learn a rule of method: the names of institutions have an official form and a consolidated translation, which you seek and do not invent. Two weeks.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. appoint the three powers of the State and their main institutions;
2. to recognise the names of ministries, parliaments and offices, including in the variants of different countries;
3. understand the official acts (law, decree, decision, agreement) and stages of their adoption;
4. understanding and rendering protocolary titles in English ( ⁧فَخَامَة⁩ , ⁧جَلَالَة⁩ , ⁧مَعَالِي⁩ , ⁧سَعَادَة⁩ );
5. translate a brief institutional statement using established translations of names.
